# Checking raw reads with FastQC {#sec-fastqc}

**Rule:** `fastqc` · **Tool:** FastQC 0.12.1 · **Input:** raw R1 and R2 FASTQ ·
**Output:** one HTML report and one zip per read file

## The problem it solves

Before spending hours aligning, you want to know whether the reads look as they should:
are the base qualities good, is there adapter, is one sequence present
millions of times? **FastQC** reads (a sample of) each FASTQ file and
draws a set of standard plots. It doesn't change your data.

## What bagPipes runs

```bash
module load fastqc/0.12.1
fastqc -o output/QC  sample_R1_001.fastq.gz  sample_R2_001.fastq.gz
# then renames the outputs to {sampleName}_R1_fastqc.html etc.
```

In bagPipes, FastQC runs on the **raw** reads, before trimming. To see the
effect of trimming you compare these plots with the Trim Galore numbers in
MultiQC.

## Reading a FastQC report

Each module gets a green tick, orange warning, or red cross. These marks
assume random genomic DNA, so **many "fails" are normal for RNA-seq**.
Interpret them; don't just count them.

| Module | What it shows | Normal for RNA-seq | Worry if... |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Per base sequence quality** | Box plot of quality at each position | High (> Q30) throughout, a gentle drop at the 3' end | Quality collapses mid-read, or R2 is much worse than R1 |
| **Per sequence quality scores** | Distribution of average read quality | One peak at high quality | A second peak at low quality |
| **Per base sequence content** | % A/C/G/T at each position | **Wobbly first ~10–12 bases** (random-hexamer priming bias): FastQC flags it, ignore it | Strong bias across the whole read |
| **Per sequence GC content** | GC % distribution vs a theoretical curve | Roughly bell-shaped; may be shifted or have shoulders | A sharp extra peak (contamination, rRNA, adapter dimer) |
| **Sequence duplication levels** | How often sequences repeat | **High duplication is expected**: highly expressed genes give many identical reads | Almost everything duplicated in a low-input library |
| **Overrepresented sequences** | Sequences making up > 0.1 % of reads | A few, often mitochondrial or rRNA | Adapter or primer dimers near the top |
| **Adapter content** | % of reads with adapter at each position | Rising toward the 3' end in libraries with short inserts | High adapter early in the read (very short inserts / dimers) |

::: {.callout-important}
## The two RNA-seq "fails" to ignore

1. **Per base sequence content** in the first ~12 bases.
2. **Sequence duplication levels.** In RNA-seq, duplication mostly reflects
   expression, not PCR. bagPipes does not remove duplicates for RNA-seq.
:::

## Try it

Everything in a *Try it* box assumes the [practice setup](practice-setup.qmd):
`source $WALK/env.sh` and `conda activate rnaseq-tools` in your terminal (on a
cluster, inside an interactive job).

```bash
mkdir -p $WALK/work/fastqc && cd $WALK/work
fastqc -o fastqc $DATA/*_001.fastq.gz          # all 8 practice files
ls fastqc
```

Open a report in your web browser:

```bash
open fastqc/N61311_untrt_R1_001_fastqc.html       # macOS
xdg-open fastqc/N61311_untrt_R1_001_fastqc.html   # Linux
```

On a cluster, copy the HTML to your laptop first (run this **on your laptop**):

```bash
scp <user>@<cluster address>:<path to>/work/fastqc/*.html .
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## Check your understanding

1. FastQC gives *Sequence duplication levels* a red cross. Should you
   re-make the library?
2. The *Adapter content* plot rises from 0 % at base 60 to 15 % at base 100.
   What does that say about your inserts?
3. Why does bagPipes run FastQC before trimming rather than after?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## Answers

1. Probably not. Duplication in RNA-seq largely reflects highly expressed
   genes. Compare across samples; one outlier is more telling than the flag.
2. About 15 % of fragments have inserts shorter than ~100 bp, so the read
   runs into adapter. Trimming will remove it.
3. To see the data as it came off the sequencer. Trim Galore's report
   (in MultiQC) then shows how much it removed.
:::
:::
